## 📋 Spec ready for review

- **Quality checklist**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md` — all items pass, no open clarifications.

### What the spec proposes

**User stories (prioritized):**
1. **P1 — Save a bookmark** (address + optional title/note). The MVP slice.
2. **P2 — Browse & find** (list newest-first, search across title/address/note).
3. **P3 — Organize with tags** (add/remove tags, filter by tag).
4. **P3 — Edit & delete** (with delete confirmation).

**13 functional requirements** covering validation, persistence, duplicate warnings, search, tags, and editing — plus edge cases (duplicates, long text, empty states) and measurable success criteria (e.g. find a bookmark among 500 in under 10s; search results under 1s at 1,000 items).

### Key scope decisions I made (please confirm or correct)

These are the choices most likely to matter — I picked sensible v1 defaults and recorded them as **Assumptions**:

| Decision | v1 assumption | Alternative |
|----------|---------------|-------------|
| Users | Single user, personal collection | Multi-user / sharing |
| Adding links | Manual entry of the address | Browser import / "save this page" extension |
| Title & preview | User supplies the title | App auto-fetches page title/preview |
| Platform | Deliberately left open until planning | Pin web / desktop / mobile now |

- **Approve** → I'll proceed to `speckit-plan` (the implementation plan). *If you want to pin a platform, that's the natural place — or tell me now and I'll fold it into the plan.*

- **Clarify** → If anything is ambiguous, I can run `speckit-clarify` to work through it with structured questions.

The plan and design artifacts are complete. **This is the planning gate — please review before I break it into tasks.**

## 📐 Plan ready for review

- **Plan**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md`
- **Research (decisions + rationale)**: `research.md`
- **Data model**: `data-model.md`
- **API contract**: `contracts/api.md`
- **Validation guide**: `quickstart.md`

### The proposed approach

**A locally-run web app** with a thin backend + browser frontend, all in TypeScript.

The one decision I want to flag explicitly, because you left platform open: **v1 is a web app you run locally, not a desktop or mobile app.** This isn't arbitrary — your must-have auto-fetch feature *forces* a backend. Browsers block fetching the title/preview from other websites (CORS), so something server-side has to do it. A backend also gives us durable storage and fast search. If you'd pictured a native desktop or mobile app, tell me now and I'll re-plan.

### Key design decisions

| Area | Decision | Why |
|------|----------|-----|
| **Capture flow** | Save *immediately*, fetch title/preview *asynchronously* | Guarantees saving is never blocked by a slow/failed page (SC-007) |
| **Metadata source** | Read the page's Open Graph / meta tags server-side | Standard, lightweight source of title + description + thumbnail; no screenshots or archiving |
| **Storage** | SQLite file + full-text search index | Zero-admin, easy to back up, sub-second search at thousands of bookmarks |
| **Duplicates** | Match on a *normalized* URL, warn but don't block | Catches "same link, slightly different form"; you can still proceed |
| **Tags** | Proper many-to-many, case-insensitive names | Clean filtering, no near-duplicate tags |

The API contract includes a requirement-coverage map so every FR-001…FR-017 traces to an endpoint.

### Your options at this gate

- **Approve** → I'll run `speckit-tasks` to generate the dependency-ordered task breakdown (still no implementation until you approve tasks too).
- **Redirect** → e.g. "make it a desktop app," "no backend, keep it simpler," or swap any technology choice, and I'll revise the plan.

All 51 tasks are implemented and marked complete. Here's the final report.

## ✅ Bookmark Manager — built and validated

The app is fully implemented against the approved spec, plan, and tasks. We went through every SDD gate: **specify → plan → tasks → implement**, with your review at each.

### What was built

**Backend** (`backend/` — Node + TypeScript + Fastify + SQLite/FTS5)
- Immediate-save + **async metadata enrichment** so a slow/failed fetch never blocks you
- Server-side title/preview fetching (Open Graph → Twitter → HTML), bounded by timeout + size cap
- URL validation, normalized-URL duplicate detection, full-text search, tags (many-to-many), edit, delete

**Frontend** (`frontend/` — React + Vite)
- Add form with optional manual title (overrides the fetched one), note, and tags; duplicate "save anyway" banner
- Bookmark cards with thumbnail/preview, `fetching…`/`failed` states, and address fallback
- Live search, tag filter, empty & no-results states, edit modal, and a delete confirmation dialog
- Short poll so auto-fetched titles appear without a manual refresh

### Validation

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Backend unit + integration tests | **37/37 pass** (URL, metadata parsing, create/dup/enrich, search, tags, edit/delete) |
| Performance (SC-003) | Search over **1,000 bookmarks in ~well under 1s** |
| Live end-to-end (real running server) | Invalid→400, create, duplicate→409, search, tag filter, edit, delete all confirmed |
| **Live auto-fetch** (the feature you asked for) | Pasted `https://example.com/` → auto-fetched real title **"Example Domain"**, status `success` ✓ |
| TypeScript typecheck (both) | Clean |
| Frontend production build | Clean (41 modules) |

### One honest caveat

The **Playwright e2e specs are written** (`frontend/tests/e2e/` — capture, browse, tags, edit-delete) but **not executed** in this environment, because it has no browsers installed and no dual-server test harness running. The equivalent flows are covered by the backend integration tests and the live curl run above. To run them yourself:

```bash
cd backend && npm run dev          # terminal 1
cd frontend && npm run dev         # terminal 2
cd frontend && npx playwright install && npm run test:e2e   # terminal 3
```

### To run the app

```bash
cd backend && npm run dev      # API on :3001
cd frontend && npm run dev     # UI on :5173  → open http://localhost:5173
```

Full details are in `README.md`. If you'd like, I can fix the flagged security-audit `npm` advisories (transitive dev deps), wire up a CI run for the e2e tests, or start on the future-work items the spec noted (browser import, one-click "save this page" capture).
